messages:
maria: heads-up — noticed different tie-break outputs from the judge runner once we switched the candidate model to int4 quant. same prompt, same seed, different winner 30% of the time. anyone else hit this?
aj: saw a couple flaky CI runs yesterday, thought it was noise. can repro locally on my linux laptop.
kevin: int4 quantization introduces tiny logit perturbations, can flip top-1 in close calls. but 30% is high — might be a downstream numerical path bug.
tara: is this only with the judge model or the whole eval pipeline?
maria: judge-only so far. eval harness shows stable scoring upstream (scores match), but the adjudication tie-breaker logic picks different winners.
sam: PR'ed a minimal repro, attaching snippet:
```bash
# repro (linux, python3.10)
python - <<'PY'
import torch
logits = torch.tensor([[0.00000001, 0.0, -1e-8]])  # tiny noise you'd get in int4 path
probs = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
print('probs:', probs.numpy())
PY
```
sam: if softmax is run in float16 or with reduced precision, ordering can flip. runner sometimes casts to fp16 for speed.
kevin: exact — runner does a fast path: quantized->dequant->fp16->softmax. float16 rounding + fused kernels can change argmax.
olivia: this affects our judge selection policy — current rubric has tie-breaker = highest average score, then random seed. we should decide deterministic tie rules for low-margin cases.
maria: propose: 1) normalize logits in fp32 before softmax 2) add epsilon clipping at 1e-6 3) deterministic tie fallback using stable sort on (score, model_name) so we avoid randomness in CI.
aj: quick patch idea: cast_logits = logits.to(torch.float32); clip = torch.clamp(cast_logits, min=-1e9, max=1e9); probs = torch.softmax(clip, dim=-1) — also force torch.manual_seed for judge model evaluation.
tara: let's add a unit test that runs with quantized weights on a couple of near-tie examples. test name: eval/runner/judge_consistency_test. CI should run that on both x86 and aarch64.
ci-bot: failing builds detected for eval/runner/judge_consistency_test on aarch64-quantized workers — opening ticket INF-2345 and tagging @eng-infra.
eval-bot: log snippet from failing job:
```
2026-02-18T14:02:31Z runner: selected winner: model-b (score 0.5123456)
2026-02-18T14:02:31Z runner: selected winner: model-a (score 0.5123454)  # same prompt, same seed across shards
```
sam: those score diffs look like fp16 rounding noise. mitigations: softmax in fp32, compute argmax in fp32, deterministic tie-break that uses lexicographic fallback.
kevin: note: doing everything fp32 hurts perf. maybe add an explicit cheap path only for judge models or near-tie cases where (top1 - top2) < delta_threshold. delta_threshold = 1e-4 ?
maria: agree. if delta < 1e-4, promote to fp32 decision path and log the event in the dashboard. that gives us a balance.
olivia: need rubric change too: update LLM-as-judge docs to record tie_procedure = [score_diff_promote, lexicographic_fallback]. i'll draft wording.
tara: also check KV cache alignment during dequant — if cache reorder happens on aarch64 that could also change incremental scores. anyone have traces?
aj: attached short trace in my repro, found a place where we do inplace ops on cached tensors in fp16. PR incoming to avoid in-place ops.
eval-bot: created trace artifact: link=https://internal-redwood/evals/1887654321/trace1 (expires in 7d)
ci-bot: tagging @eng-infra and @eng-runtime to spin a few quantized runners with deterministic seeds for the next CI sweep.
maria: plan of action: 1) land non-inplace patch (aj) 2) add fp32 promotion for near-ties (kevin + sam) 3) add judge_consistency_test in CI (tara) 4) update rubric tie-handling (olivia) 5) dashboard metric: evals/judge/consistency (agreement_rate, kappa, tie_rate).
olivia: I'll update the rubric draft and drop it in #docs once written. will add an example tie case for annotators.
kevin: I'll benchmark perf impact of fp32 promotion on a small sample and report back.
sam: pushed a unit test that simulates int4 dequant jitter — failing currently, will iterate.
maria: thanks team. small follow-up: if we end up promoting too often we'll tune threshold - keep logs so we can pick a cost vs stability point. :thumbsup:
aj: can we add a lightweight flag to runner: JUDGE_DETERMINISTIC=1 to force stable tie resolution for canary runs?
maria: yes, add env var and wire into canary job template.
ci-bot: INF-2345 updated: 'add deterministic judge path and consistency tests' — assigned to eng-runtime and eng-infra.
olivia: tagging legal/compliance for note (we need deterministic adjudication for some regulated customers).
tara: moving this to a tiny RFC in the eval docs after the patches.
maria: perfect. will keep thread updated with PR links and metrics once CI runs are green.
